Privacy & transparency

Privacy Policy

This page explains what Math Center Calculator stores in your browser, how calculation history and preferences work, what this standalone version is designed not to collect, and what you should consider when using a hosted copy.

Effective date: 10 October 2026 · Version: 1.2
Quick summary: In the supplied standalone calculator file, your profile name, calculation history, and accent-color preference are stored in your browser's local storage. The calculator page is configured with a restrictive Content Security Policy that blocks network connections from that page in supporting browsers. This does not control separate hosting-provider logs, browser extensions, device monitoring, or changes made to the code by someone else.

1. Scope of this policy

This Privacy Policy applies to the Math Center Calculator ("MCC", "Math Center Calculator", "the app", "we", "us", or "our") standalone HTML calculator supplied with this policy. It describes the intended behavior of that version, including calculator inputs, displayed results, calculation history, the profile-name prompt, and color preferences.

The policy may not accurately describe a modified, rebranded, embedded, or third-party copy. If you received MCC from a website, app store, school, employer, or another publisher, that publisher may add services or practices that are not part of the standalone file. Read any additional notices that publisher provides.

This document is intended to explain the app in plain language. It is not legal advice and does not create guarantees that cannot be verified in your particular browser, device, or deployment.

Standalone HTMLBrowser-based storageNo account system in this version

2. Information stored or entered

The app may process or store the following information so its features can work:

Data typePurposeWhere it is stored

Please do not enter passwords, payment-card numbers, government identification numbers, confidential business information, or other sensitive personal information into calculator fields. The app is a general-purpose calculator, not a secure vault.

3. How browser local storage works

The supplied version uses the browser's localStorage to remember the display name, calculation history and color preference. This storage is associated with the page's origin when hosted on a website, or with the browser's handling of a local file. It is not the same as an account or a cloud database.

  • Data usually remains after you close and reopen the browser until you clear it or the browser removes it.
  • People who can use the same browser profile or device may be able to access the saved information.
  • Browser extensions, malware, developer tools, or a person with access to the device may be able to read or change local data.
  • Private/incognito browsing may handle or clear storage differently depending on the browser.
  • Browser settings, storage limits, or device cleanup tools can cause saved data to be unavailable or deleted.
Local does not mean encrypted. The app does not provide a password-protected vault or promise that local storage is encrypted. Do not use it to store confidential calculations on a shared device.

4. Calculator inputs and results

Calculations are performed by JavaScript within the supplied page. The app uses your entered values to compute and display a result. When you complete a calculation, the app's history feature saves a record containing the calculator's name, category, result and displayed time. The supplied version does not intentionally save every raw input field value as part of that history record.

Some results can indirectly reveal information about the values you entered. For example, a result and calculator name might disclose a budget estimate, measurement, or other fact. If that could be sensitive, clear history after use and avoid shared devices.

Results are provided for convenience and may be affected by rounding, formula assumptions, missing context, or software errors. Verify important calculations independently before relying on them for financial, engineering, medical, legal, academic, or safety-critical decisions.

5. Network connections, analytics and tracking

The supplied calculator HTML includes a restrictive Content Security Policy. In browsers that enforce it, the calculator page's policy blocks outgoing network connections from the page and disallows external scripts, frames, objects, and media sources. The supplied calculator source does not intentionally include analytics scripts, advertising pixels, or third-party tracking scripts.

Optional voice input: If you choose the microphone feature, the browser Speech Recognition service may process audio or a transcript using the browser provider’s systems, depending on browser and settings. This is separate from typed calculator input, and MCC cannot verify the provider’s processing or retention. Use typed input if you do not want to invoke browser speech recognition.

These statements describe the supplied file, not every website on which it might be hosted. When you download or open a hosted page, the web server, content-delivery network, domain provider, security service, or platform may receive ordinary connection information such as IP address, request time, requested path, browser user agent, referrer information (subject to browser policy), and security logs. Such processing occurs at the infrastructure level and is governed by the relevant provider's policies and configuration.

A browser extension, injected script, modified copy, compromised device, or altered hosting setup may behave differently. A Content Security Policy is an important defense, not proof that all possible data collection is impossible.

6. Cookies and similar technologies

The supplied calculator uses browser local storage for its own saved preferences and history; it does not need an account cookie for the core calculator functions. The standalone file does not intentionally set advertising or analytics cookies.

If you use MCC through a hosting platform, that platform or its infrastructure may use cookies or similar technologies for security, load balancing, analytics, or other site operations. Check the hosting provider's notice for details. This policy does not describe cookies used by unrelated websites you visit through your browser.

7. Sharing, sale and disclosure

The supplied standalone calculator is not designed to send your profile name, calculation history, or color preference to a remote MCC server. The supplied version has no built-in user account, social sharing, payment, or cloud-sync feature for these local records.

We do not claim that data held on your device is inaccessible to everyone else. Anyone who can access your browser profile or device may have access to it. A hosting provider may separately process server logs as described above. If a modified version adds accounts, cloud backup, support forms, advertising, analytics, payment processing, or synchronization, the privacy practices and disclosures must be updated before those features are used.

This standalone file is not designed to sell local calculation history or profile data. It cannot make promises on behalf of third-party hosting providers, browser vendors, device manufacturers, or publishers who distribute modified copies.

8. Data retention and deletion

Calculation history is limited to the most recent 300 records in the supplied version. The profile name and accent-color preference are kept in local storage until removed by the app, browser, or user. There is no MCC cloud account in this version from which we can centrally delete your local data.

How to remove locally saved data

  1. Open MCC in the same browser profile where you used it.
  2. Use the app's History control and choose Clear to remove saved calculation-history records.
  3. For the saved display name and color preference, clear the site's storage through your browser's site-data controls. For a local HTML file, browser storage behavior may vary by browser and file origin.
  4. If you are unsure, consult your browser's official help for clearing site data. Clearing all site data may remove other preferences or saved information for that origin too.

Deleting browser data does not remove server logs that a hosting provider may already have retained, backups outside the app, or information held by a third-party service.

9. Security measures and limitations

The supplied calculator includes several defensive measures, including a restrictive Content Security Policy, a Permissions Policy that denies selected browser capabilities, validation of stored history records, limits on some stored values, and escaping of text shown in the interface. These measures reduce certain risks but do not make the application invulnerable.

  • Keep your browser and operating system updated.
  • Use a separate browser profile on shared computers and lock your device when away.
  • Do not use a device that you suspect is compromised for confidential work.
  • Download the HTML only from a source you trust and review changes before running a modified copy.
  • If you publish the app, configure security headers at the web server or hosting platform as appropriate; HTML meta policies do not replace every HTTP response header.

No method of storing or transmitting information is perfectly secure. The app cannot protect information from all malware, malicious extensions, physical access, browser vulnerabilities, or operating-system compromise.

10. Children and age-related privacy

MCC is a general-purpose calculator and is not designed to solicit personal information from children. The app asks for a display name to personalize the interface; you may choose a nickname rather than a full legal name. Parents or guardians should supervise younger users when they share devices or use hosted versions.

If you believe a child has entered personal information into a hosted version and you need help removing it, use the contact channel provided by the publisher or hosting provider. For the standalone file, the data is generally controlled through the browser storage on the device where it was entered.

11. Your choices and privacy controls

You can choose what to enter, whether to use calculation history, and whether to retain the saved profile name and color preference. Available controls depend on the exact version you are using.

  • Minimize: Use a nickname and avoid entering sensitive information.
  • Review: Open the History panel to see records stored by the app.
  • Clear history: Use the Clear control in the History panel.
  • Reset preferences: Clear local site data in your browser to remove the saved name and accent color.
  • Stop using the app: Close the page; if desired, remove its local storage through browser settings.

Depending on your location and the way MCC is hosted, you may have legal rights to request access, correction, deletion, objection, restriction, or other privacy remedies. Because this standalone version does not maintain a central account database of your local records, those rights may need to be exercised through your device or the relevant hosting provider. This policy does not limit any rights that applicable law grants you.

12. Third-party services and external links

The supplied standalone calculator is intended to work without third-party scripts or external services for its core calculations. If a distributor adds links, ads, embedded content, authentication, cloud services, analytics, or payment processing, those services may collect information under their own policies.

We do not control the privacy, security, or content practices of independent third parties. Review their notices before sharing information with them. The appearance of a third-party name or link in a modified version does not mean that the standalone MCC file operates or controls that service.

13. Hosting, downloads and server logs

When MCC is hosted publicly, a hosting provider may automatically process technical request information to deliver the file, protect the service, troubleshoot errors, prevent abuse, or measure service reliability. Typical server-side logs can include IP address, timestamp, requested resource, status code, and user-agent information. The exact fields and retention periods depend on the provider and configuration.

The app's page-level network restrictions do not prevent a server from receiving the initial request needed to deliver a hosted file. If you download the file and run it locally, the host may still have logged the download request, but the app's later calculations are processed in the local page in the supplied version.

For questions about hosting logs, review the privacy and data-retention information published by the service that hosts your copy. If you are the site operator, provide your own accurate contact details, data-controller identity where required, and any required legal disclosures.

14. International use and legal compliance

You may access MCC from different countries or regions. Privacy laws and terminology vary by location. This policy describes the behavior of the supplied standalone file at a general level and is not a statement that every legal obligation is satisfied in every jurisdiction.

If you operate or distribute MCC commercially, you are responsible for reviewing the laws that apply to your audience and deployment, including any rules on privacy notices, children's data, cookies, consumer disclosures, accessibility, and data security. Update this policy to reflect the actual operator, actual data practices, and local legal requirements.

15. Changes to this policy

This policy may be updated when the app changes, new features are added, hosting arrangements change, or legal requirements evolve. The effective date at the top indicates the date of this document version. A newer version should describe material changes clearly.

If new features introduce remote data collection, accounts, cloud synchronization, analytics, advertising, or payments, the operator should update this policy before enabling those features and provide any notices or choices required by law. Do not rely on this policy for a substantially modified version without reviewing it.

16. Contact and privacy requests

If this page is published as part of an official MCC website, the site operator should provide a monitored contact address or privacy-request form here. No verified privacy contact details were supplied with this standalone file, so this template intentionally does not invent an email address, phone number, business address, or legal entity.

Site owner action: Before publishing commercially, replace this paragraph with the real operator name and a monitored contact method. If applicable law requires a data controller, representative, grievance officer, or other contact, include the accurate details and process.

If you are using a copy distributed by someone else, contact that publisher or the hosting platform for questions about its deployment and data practices.

17. Important notice

This document is a privacy-policy template describing the supplied MCC HTML file based on its visible implementation. It is not a legal opinion, security certification, audit of the hosting environment, or guarantee that every distributed copy behaves identically. The site owner should verify the final code and hosting configuration and obtain qualified legal advice when needed.

In case of a conflict between this page and the actual behavior of a modified version, the operator must investigate and update the notice so that it accurately reflects the product. Never describe a feature as local-only, anonymous, encrypted, or free of tracking unless the complete deployed system supports that statement.

18. Data-flow overview

This section gives a practical overview of how information moves through the supplied standalone HTML version. It describes the intended flow of the delivered file, not every browser, device, operating-system, hosting, or network process outside the app's control.

When you first open the page

If you open a hosted copy, your browser first requests the HTML document from the hosting service. That request necessarily reaches the server that delivers the file and may be recorded in ordinary server logs. If you open a downloaded copy, the initial download may already have been recorded by the site or service from which you obtained it. Once the supplied page is running, its restrictive page policy is designed to block the page from making network connections.

When you enter a value

Calculator inputs are used by the page's JavaScript to calculate a displayed result. The supplied version is not designed to send the entered values to a remote calculator service. Avoid treating this design as permission to enter confidential data: the browser, device, extensions, screen recording tools, accessibility tools, or other software on the device may operate independently of the app.

When you save history or preferences

The app may write a limited set of values, including the display name, calculation history and accent-color preference, to browser local storage. This storage remains on the browser/device environment rather than being placed in an MCC account database by the supplied version. A person who has access to the same browser profile may also have access to those values.

When you clear history

The History control removes the calculation-history records that the app manages. Clearing history does not automatically remove every other local preference, browser cache, operating-system backup, browser sync copy, screenshot, or hosting log. Use the browser's own site-data controls if you also want to remove the saved name and color preference.

ActionExpected app behaviorWhat may be outside app control
Open hosted pageLoads the calculator page.Hosting provider request logs and network infrastructure.
Perform a calculationComputes and displays a result in the page.Device monitoring, extensions, screenshots or other software.
Save historyStores supported history records locally in the browser.Access by other users of the same browser profile or device.
Change theme colorSaves the color preference locally.Browser storage cleanup, profile sync behavior or device access.
Clear historyRemoves history records managed by the app.Other storage, copies, screenshots and provider logs.

19. Legal bases and purposes

Where a privacy law requires a legal basis for personal-data processing, the appropriate basis depends on who operates the copy, where the operator and user are located, and which features are enabled. The supplied standalone file does not identify a legal entity or establish a universal legal basis for every possible deployment. The following are explanations for a site operator to review, not a claim that a particular legal basis applies in every situation.

  • Providing the calculator: processing values you enter so the page can return the calculation you requested may be necessary to provide the feature you chose to use.
  • Remembering your preferences: local storage of a name or theme preference may support the function you expect when you revisit the page. If local-storage consent or notice rules apply to your deployment, the operator should provide the required choice or notice.
  • Maintaining security: a hosting provider may process technical logs to deliver files, prevent abuse, diagnose faults, or protect infrastructure, according to its own terms and applicable law.
  • Legal obligations: an operator may need to retain or disclose limited information where required by a valid legal obligation. Such obligations do not arise from the standalone HTML file itself.

The supplied page is not designed to create a marketing profile, run targeted advertising, sell local calculation history, or build a cross-site identity. If the operator later adds advertising, analytics, account services, cloud storage, remote AI, payments, or other integrations, the operator must reassess the data flows and legal bases before activating those features.

20. Privacy requests process

Because the supplied version stores its main saved preferences and history in the browser, there is generally no central MCC account record for an operator to search, correct, or delete on your behalf. You can usually inspect and remove this information directly in the same browser profile. A hosted website operator may still hold technical server logs or other records associated with site operation.

How to make a request to the correct party

  1. Identify whether you are using the original standalone file, a copy hosted on an MCC website, or a modified version distributed by another party.
  2. For local name, color, and history data, use the app controls and browser site-data settings described in Section 8.
  3. For server logs or information held by a website operator, contact the operator using its published privacy contact details.
  4. For information held by a third-party host or service, consult that provider's privacy notice and request process.
  5. Describe the request clearly, but do not send passwords, payment details, government ID numbers, or other unnecessary sensitive information in an ordinary email.

Depending on applicable law, requests may include access, correction, deletion, portability, objection, restriction, or withdrawal of consent. The scope, deadlines, identity-verification requirements and exceptions differ by jurisdiction. An operator should respond according to the law that actually applies and should not request more identity information than is reasonably necessary to process the request safely.

If an operator cannot locate a requested item because it was never collected centrally or has already been deleted, it should explain that limitation accurately. This policy does not remove or reduce any mandatory rights provided by applicable law.

21. Security incident and breach response

The app includes technical protections, but no software or hosting arrangement can promise zero risk. A security incident could involve unauthorized device access, a compromised hosting account, a malicious modified copy, a vulnerable browser, or exposure of data held by a separate provider. The appropriate response depends on the incident and the party that controls the affected system.

If you believe information has been exposed, stop entering sensitive information, close the page if appropriate, and secure the affected device and browser account. If the issue concerns a hosted website, notify that site's operator using its verified contact channel. If the issue concerns a browser extension, operating system, or hosting account, contact the relevant provider as well.

A site operator should have a proportionate incident-response plan that includes assessing the facts, containing the issue, preserving necessary evidence, correcting the cause, and determining whether notices to affected users or authorities are required by law. The operator should not state that a breach occurred—or that no breach occurred—without an appropriate factual basis.

The standalone file does not provide a centralized breach-detection service, account monitoring, device antivirus, or incident-response team. Any such services would need to be separately provided and accurately described.

22. Data accuracy, integrity and calculation limitations

Personal data and calculation values can be inaccurate because of typing errors, unexpected input formats, rounding, browser differences, or a defect in a calculator formula. The app is a general-purpose utility and should not be treated as the authoritative record for a financial, legal, medical, engineering, tax, academic assessment, or safety-critical decision.

  • Check the units, signs, decimal places, dates and assumptions you enter.
  • Review the displayed result before copying or relying on it.
  • For high-impact decisions, verify the method and result independently using a trusted source or qualified professional.
  • Do not assume that a history entry is a complete audit trail. History may retain a displayed summary rather than every original input, assumption, or intermediate step.
  • Do not assume a result is backed up. Browser storage can be cleared, corrupted, unavailable, or lost when a profile or device changes.

Where the app displays a history item, the stored value is intended to help you recall recent use. It is not a certified financial ledger, immutable log, official invoice, or proof that a transaction occurred. Users remain responsible for checking important calculations and retaining any records they legally or practically need.

23. Accessibility, shared devices and account safety

Privacy depends partly on how a device is shared and configured. If you use MCC on a school, library, workplace, family, internet-café, or other shared computer, someone else may be able to open the same browser profile and see saved history or preferences. Clearing the app's history is helpful but does not remove screenshots, downloaded copies, clipboard contents, browser-level records, or information saved by other software.

  • Prefer a separate operating-system or browser profile when a device is shared.
  • Sign out of the browser profile itself when finished, where applicable.
  • Do not save sensitive information in names, calculator fields, or history summaries.
  • Review browser extensions and install only extensions you trust.
  • Lock your device when you leave it unattended.
  • If using a public computer, consider closing the page and clearing site data after use, while remembering that public-device administrators may have other monitoring capabilities.

Accessibility features, screen readers, clipboard managers, keyboard utilities, remote-desktop software, and device-level assistive technologies may process what appears on screen or what you copy. Those tools are outside the calculator's direct control and may have their own privacy settings. This notice is not intended to discourage accessibility tools; it is a reminder to review settings on shared or sensitive devices.

24. Responsibilities of website owners and distributors

If you publish, host, rebrand, embed, or distribute MCC, you become responsible for checking that your deployed product and this notice match. The supplied privacy policy is a starting point for transparency; it is not a substitute for the operator's own legal review or operational controls.

Before launch, a site operator should:

  • Identify the actual person or organization operating the service and provide a monitored privacy contact.
  • Check the final HTML, JavaScript, headers, hosting configuration, and every third-party integration.
  • Remove statements that no longer match the product, including claims about local storage, network restrictions, accounts, analytics, or retention.
  • Explain any hosting logs, support inboxes, analytics, advertising, payment processors, cloud storage, AI endpoints, or account databases that are actually used.
  • Set and verify appropriate HTTP security headers on the live HTTPS site. A meta policy inside HTML does not replace all response headers.
  • Set realistic retention periods for logs and support records, restrict staff access, and document who can access information.
  • Provide any required notices, consent controls, grievance contact, representative, children's privacy process, or other disclosures for the applicable jurisdiction.
  • Review the policy whenever the product, operator, hosting provider, or data practices change.

Do not claim that data is encrypted, anonymous, deleted permanently, inaccessible to all third parties, or impossible to leak unless those statements have been verified for the entire relevant system. A browser-only design can reduce remote data flows, but it cannot control every component of the user's device or the hosting environment.

25. Definitions

  • App or supplied version: the standalone Math Center Calculator HTML file distributed with this policy, as distinct from a modified or integrated version.
  • Browser local storage: a browser feature that lets a website origin save small amounts of data on the user's device. It is not automatically encrypted and is not the same as cloud storage.
  • Calculation history: the list of recent calculation summaries the app saves to help a user recall prior results.
  • Personal information or personal data: information that identifies, relates to, describes, or can reasonably be linked to an identifiable person under the law that applies.
  • Hosting provider: a company or service that delivers the page or files to a browser and may process technical request information.
  • Third party: a person, company, service, or organization separate from the user and the operator of the copy being used.
  • Security header: an instruction delivered by a web server with an HTTP response to help browsers handle content more safely. Some security behaviors cannot be fully enforced using HTML meta tags alone.
  • Modified copy: a version whose code, hosting, integrations, storage behavior, branding, or data collection differs from the supplied standalone file.

These definitions are included for readability and may not replace formal definitions in the privacy laws applicable to a particular deployment.

26. Publication checklist

This policy should be reviewed before it is presented as the final legal notice for a public website. Use the checklist below to verify the real deployment rather than assuming that a local test guarantees the behavior of the published website.

  • Confirm that the displayed operator name and privacy contact are correct.
  • Confirm which fields are written to local storage and how the app's Clear History feature behaves.
  • Confirm that the deployed version does not include unlisted analytics, external scripts, remote fonts, remote APIs, advertising pixels, or embedded services.
  • Check the actual HTTP response headers on the live site, including Content Security Policy, Referrer Policy, Permissions Policy and framing restrictions.
  • Review the host's own logging, retention, support and abuse-prevention practices.
  • Verify whether local-storage notice or consent requirements apply to the intended audience.
  • Update this page if accounts, cloud synchronization, remote AI, payments, subscriptions, telemetry, or third-party integrations are introduced.
  • Provide accessible ways to read the policy and contact the operator.
  • Keep a dated copy of each material policy revision and make material changes understandable to users.
  • Seek qualified legal advice when the app is used commercially, processes children's data, or serves users in jurisdictions with specific privacy requirements.
Important for operators: A privacy policy describes practices; it does not itself create technical privacy protections. Configure the software and hosting to match the promises made here.

27. Plain-language summary

The supplied MCC file is designed to perform calculations in the browser and to keep a limited set of preferences and history records in browser local storage. It is not designed to send calculator inputs or saved local history to an MCC cloud database. The page includes restrictions intended to prevent its own code from initiating network connections in supporting browsers.

However, opening a hosted page can generate server logs, browser extensions and device software operate independently, local storage is not an encrypted vault, and a modified version may behave differently. You can clear history in the app and remove saved preferences through browser site-data settings. If you need to ask about hosting records, contact the operator of the website where you accessed the page.

Use a nickname if you prefer not to enter your real name, avoid sensitive information, keep your device secure, and independently verify results that matter. The site operator must keep this policy aligned with the actual deployed version and applicable law.

User guide · Step by step

How to use
Math Center Calculator

Find a calculator, enter your values, calculate your answer, and manage your preferences. This guide explains the main features in plain language.

Open Calculator Center →Start with the guide

On this page

1. Quick start2. Search calculators3. Categories & sorting4. Calculate an answer5. Example calculations6. Random calculator7. Accent colors8. History9. Privacy & data10. Troubleshooting11. Tips for accurate results12. FAQ

1. Quick start

  1. Open this MCC Professional HTML file in a modern browser such as Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari.
  2. On the welcome screen, choose Open Calculator Center, try a random calculator, or search for a tool.
  3. If the app asks for a name, enter a display name and select Continue. The app uses this to personalize the greeting.
  4. Find the calculator you need and select Open Calculator.
  5. Fill in the requested values, then select Calculate. Read the result shown in the result panel.
Quick tip: You do not need to scroll through every tool. Searching by calculator name or a formula is usually faster.

2. Search for a calculator

Use the search box on the welcome screen or in the calculator center. Search can match calculator names, categories, and formula text.

  1. Click or tap the search field.
  2. Type a term such as percentage, circle area, loan EMI, average, or a formula term.
  3. The calculator list updates to show matching tools.
  4. Select ✕ Clear to remove the search and show the broader list again.

If no results appear, try a shorter term, a related word, or select the “All” category.

3. Use categories and sorting

Categories help narrow the library to a topic. Available groups include Basic Math, Algebra, Geometry, Finance, Statistics, Physics, Chemistry, Electrical, Business, Time & Date, Construction, Data & Digital, and Health & Everyday.

  • Select a category chip to filter the library.
  • Select All to see calculators across categories.
  • Use the Sort menu to view names A–Z, Z–A, or categories alphabetically.
  • Each calculator card shows its category and a formula summary before you open it.
For school mathsTry Basic Math, Algebra, Geometry or Statistics.
For everyday planningTry Finance, Time & Date, Business or Health & Everyday.

4. Enter values and calculate

  1. Open a calculator card. A calculator window appears with its name and formula.
  2. Read the field labels carefully. Different calculators require different inputs, often labelled A, B, C, or with a more specific name.
  3. Enter numeric values in each required field. Use a decimal point for decimal values, for example 2.5.
  4. Select Calculate. In supported forms, pressing Enter also starts the calculation.
  5. Read the answer in the result area. Check the units and formula to confirm that the tool matches your task.
  6. Select Reset if you want to clear the current inputs and start again. Use the close button to return to the calculator list.
Important: Do not leave required fields blank. Some formulas also require non-zero denominators or valid ranges. If a message appears, correct the input and calculate again.

5. Example calculations

Example A — Percentage out of total

To calculate marks percentage, open Percentage (Out of 100), enter obtained marks in Marks / Value Obtained. The total defaults to 100 and can be changed. For 45 out of 50, the result is 90%. For 45 out of 100, the result is 45%. Formula: obtained ÷ total × 100.

Example B — Rectangle area

Open Rectangle Area. Enter the rectangle’s length and width in the corresponding fields. The formula is A × B. For 8 and 3, the area is 24 square units.

Example C — Circle area

Open Circle Area and enter the radius. The formula is πr². For radius 2, the area is approximately 12.566 square units.

Examples illustrate the formulas; always follow the actual labels shown in the calculator window because field labels vary by tool.

6. Try a random calculator

Select Random on the welcome screen or calculator center to open a randomly selected calculator. This is useful for exploring the library when you are not sure which tool to try.

If the random selection is not useful, close it and use search or categories to choose a specific calculator.

7. Change the accent color

  1. In the calculator center, select Colors.
  2. Choose from the 50,000 accent colors using paginated swatches, or use the custom color picker.
  3. If you know a HEX color, enter a value such as #2563eb in the HEX field.
  4. Select Apply Custom Color to apply a valid custom color.
  5. Close the color window to return to the calculator list.

The accent color changes the interface highlights. It does not change a calculator’s mathematical formula or result.

8. View and clear calculation history

Select History to view saved calculation records available in this browser. The app keeps a limited local history.

  • Use the history window to review previous entries.
  • Select Clear if you want to remove the saved history.
  • Clearing browser site data or local storage can also remove the saved history and profile preferences.
  • History saved in one browser profile is not automatically synced to another browser, device, or person.
Shared computer? Clear history and remove any saved profile information you do not want the next person using the same browser profile to see.

9. Privacy and data

The calculator is designed to perform calculations in the page and store its profile, selected accent color, and limited history in the browser’s local storage. It does not intentionally send calculator inputs to a remote server in the supplied local version. However, privacy depends on your device, browser, extensions, and how you host or modify the file.

  • Do not enter passwords, payment card details, identity numbers, or other sensitive information into calculator fields.
  • On a shared device, other people who use the same browser profile may be able to access locally stored information.
  • Keep your browser and operating system updated and use only a copy of the app you trust.
  • Read the Privacy Policy for more information about local storage, security limits, and privacy choices.

10. Troubleshooting

The calculator list is empty or search finds nothing

Select All, clear the search field, and try a shorter term. Refresh the page if the list still does not appear.

The result is not what I expected

Check that you opened the intended calculator, used the correct units, entered values in the correct fields, and interpreted the formula correctly. Compare with a trusted source for important calculations.

The app rejects an input

Enter a valid number, fill required fields, and avoid values that make a denominator zero or a formula undefined. For date, finance, or science calculations, check the expected input format and units.

History or colors did not stay after closing the browser

The browser may have cleared local site data, be using private browsing, or block local storage. Try a normal browser window and avoid clearing site data if you want to retain local preferences.

The page looks different on another device

Local settings are stored separately by browser and device. The page layout may also adapt to the screen size.

A link to the guide or privacy page does not open

The user guide and privacy policy are included in this same HTML file. Use the in-page links to return to the calculator, open the guide, or read the privacy policy.

11. Tips for accurate results

  • Confirm the formula: Read the formula summary before using a tool.
  • Use consistent units: Do not mix metres with centimetres or monthly rates with annual rates unless the formula expects conversion.
  • Check your inputs: A misplaced decimal point can change the result substantially.
  • Understand rounding: Displayed precision may differ from a result rounded by hand.
  • Verify important decisions: For taxes, loans, engineering, health, or legal and financial decisions, confirm results with an appropriate professional or authoritative source.
  • Remember the scope: A calculator provides a result from its implemented formula; it does not automatically verify whether your assumptions are correct.

12. Frequently asked questions

Do I need to create an online account?

The supplied local version asks for a display name, but it does not provide a cloud account or cross-device syncing.

Can I use the calculator without an internet connection?

The HTML file itself is local and is designed without remote API calls. Availability can still depend on the browser and how you open or host the file.

Will changing the color change my answer?

No. Accent colors are an appearance preference and should not affect the calculator formulas.

How do I reset a calculator?

Open the calculator and choose Reset. This resets its current inputs; it is different from clearing the saved history.

Where can I read about privacy?

Use the Privacy Policy link. For privacy questions, contact the site owner using contact information they have published.

Ready to begin? Open the calculator center, search for your tool, enter the values carefully, and check the result against the formula shown.

Privacy & transparency

Privacy Policy

This page explains what Math Center Calculator stores in your browser, how calculation history and preferences work, what this standalone version is designed not to collect, and what you should consider when using a hosted copy.

Effective date: 10 October 2026 · Version: 1.2
Quick summary: In the supplied standalone calculator file, your profile name, calculation history, and accent-color preference are stored in your browser's local storage. The calculator page is configured with a restrictive Content Security Policy that blocks network connections from that page in supporting browsers. This does not control separate hosting-provider logs, browser extensions, device monitoring, or changes made to the code by someone else.

1. Scope of this policy

This Privacy Policy applies to the Math Center Calculator ("MCC", "Math Center Calculator", "the app", "we", "us", or "our") standalone HTML calculator supplied with this policy. It describes the intended behavior of that version, including calculator inputs, displayed results, calculation history, the profile-name prompt, and color preferences.

The policy may not accurately describe a modified, rebranded, embedded, or third-party copy. If you received MCC from a website, app store, school, employer, or another publisher, that publisher may add services or practices that are not part of the standalone file. Read any additional notices that publisher provides.

This document is intended to explain the app in plain language. It is not legal advice and does not create guarantees that cannot be verified in your particular browser, device, or deployment.

Standalone HTMLBrowser-based storageNo account system in this version

2. Information stored or entered

The app may process or store the following information so its features can work:

Data typePurposeWhere it is stored
Profile/display namePersonalizes the greeting in the app. The app limits the name to 40 characters.Browser local storage
Calculation historyShows recent calculation names, results, categories and displayed timestamps. Up to 300 history records are retained by the app.Browser local storage
Accent-color preferenceRemembers your chosen color theme.Browser local storage
Calculator inputsUsed to calculate the result you request.Processed by the page while you use it; inputs are not intentionally added to history as raw field values by the supplied version.
Search text and selected categoryFilters the calculator list while you use the page.In page memory during the current session, unless a modified version adds persistence.

Please do not enter passwords, payment-card numbers, government identification numbers, confidential business information, or other sensitive personal information into calculator fields. The app is a general-purpose calculator, not a secure vault.

3. How browser local storage works

The supplied version uses the browser's localStorage to remember the display name, calculation history and color preference. This storage is associated with the page's origin when hosted on a website, or with the browser's handling of a local file. It is not the same as an account or a cloud database.

  • Data usually remains after you close and reopen the browser until you clear it or the browser removes it.
  • People who can use the same browser profile or device may be able to access the saved information.
  • Browser extensions, malware, developer tools, or a person with access to the device may be able to read or change local data.
  • Private/incognito browsing may handle or clear storage differently depending on the browser.
  • Browser settings, storage limits, or device cleanup tools can cause saved data to be unavailable or deleted.
Local does not mean encrypted. The app does not provide a password-protected vault or promise that local storage is encrypted. Do not use it to store confidential calculations on a shared device.

4. Calculator inputs and results

Calculations are performed by JavaScript within the supplied page. The app uses your entered values to compute and display a result. When you complete a calculation, the app's history feature saves a record containing the calculator's name, category, result and displayed time. The supplied version does not intentionally save every raw input field value as part of that history record.

Some results can indirectly reveal information about the values you entered. For example, a result and calculator name might disclose a budget estimate, measurement, or other fact. If that could be sensitive, clear history after use and avoid shared devices.

Results are provided for convenience and may be affected by rounding, formula assumptions, missing context, or software errors. Verify important calculations independently before relying on them for financial, engineering, medical, legal, academic, or safety-critical decisions.

5. Network connections, analytics and tracking

The supplied calculator HTML includes a restrictive Content Security Policy. In browsers that enforce it, the calculator page's policy blocks outgoing network connections from the page and disallows external scripts, frames, objects, and media sources. The supplied calculator source does not intentionally include analytics scripts, advertising pixels, or third-party tracking scripts.

Optional voice input: If you choose the microphone feature, the browser Speech Recognition service may process audio or a transcript using the browser provider’s systems, depending on browser and settings. This is separate from typed calculator input, and MCC cannot verify the provider’s processing or retention. Use typed input if you do not want to invoke browser speech recognition.

These statements describe the supplied file, not every website on which it might be hosted. When you download or open a hosted page, the web server, content-delivery network, domain provider, security service, or platform may receive ordinary connection information such as IP address, request time, requested path, browser user agent, referrer information (subject to browser policy), and security logs. Such processing occurs at the infrastructure level and is governed by the relevant provider's policies and configuration.

A browser extension, injected script, modified copy, compromised device, or altered hosting setup may behave differently. A Content Security Policy is an important defense, not proof that all possible data collection is impossible.

6. Cookies and similar technologies

The supplied calculator uses browser local storage for its own saved preferences and history; it does not need an account cookie for the core calculator functions. The standalone file does not intentionally set advertising or analytics cookies.

If you use MCC through a hosting platform, that platform or its infrastructure may use cookies or similar technologies for security, load balancing, analytics, or other site operations. Check the hosting provider's notice for details. This policy does not describe cookies used by unrelated websites you visit through your browser.

7. Sharing, sale and disclosure

The supplied standalone calculator is not designed to send your profile name, calculation history, or color preference to a remote MCC server. The supplied version has no built-in user account, social sharing, payment, or cloud-sync feature for these local records.

We do not claim that data held on your device is inaccessible to everyone else. Anyone who can access your browser profile or device may have access to it. A hosting provider may separately process server logs as described above. If a modified version adds accounts, cloud backup, support forms, advertising, analytics, payment processing, or synchronization, the privacy practices and disclosures must be updated before those features are used.

This standalone file is not designed to sell local calculation history or profile data. It cannot make promises on behalf of third-party hosting providers, browser vendors, device manufacturers, or publishers who distribute modified copies.

8. Data retention and deletion

Calculation history is limited to the most recent 300 records in the supplied version. The profile name and accent-color preference are kept in local storage until removed by the app, browser, or user. There is no MCC cloud account in this version from which we can centrally delete your local data.

How to remove locally saved data

  1. Open MCC in the same browser profile where you used it.
  2. Use the app's History control and choose Clear to remove saved calculation-history records.
  3. For the saved display name and color preference, clear the site's storage through your browser's site-data controls. For a local HTML file, browser storage behavior may vary by browser and file origin.
  4. If you are unsure, consult your browser's official help for clearing site data. Clearing all site data may remove other preferences or saved information for that origin too.

Deleting browser data does not remove server logs that a hosting provider may already have retained, backups outside the app, or information held by a third-party service.

9. Security measures and limitations

The supplied calculator includes several defensive measures, including a restrictive Content Security Policy, a Permissions Policy that denies selected browser capabilities, validation of stored history records, limits on some stored values, and escaping of text shown in the interface. These measures reduce certain risks but do not make the application invulnerable.

  • Keep your browser and operating system updated.
  • Use a separate browser profile on shared computers and lock your device when away.
  • Do not use a device that you suspect is compromised for confidential work.
  • Download the HTML only from a source you trust and review changes before running a modified copy.
  • If you publish the app, configure security headers at the web server or hosting platform as appropriate; HTML meta policies do not replace every HTTP response header.

No method of storing or transmitting information is perfectly secure. The app cannot protect information from all malware, malicious extensions, physical access, browser vulnerabilities, or operating-system compromise.

10. Children and age-related privacy

MCC is a general-purpose calculator and is not designed to solicit personal information from children. The app asks for a display name to personalize the interface; you may choose a nickname rather than a full legal name. Parents or guardians should supervise younger users when they share devices or use hosted versions.

If you believe a child has entered personal information into a hosted version and you need help removing it, use the contact channel provided by the publisher or hosting provider. For the standalone file, the data is generally controlled through the browser storage on the device where it was entered.

11. Your choices and privacy controls

You can choose what to enter, whether to use calculation history, and whether to retain the saved profile name and color preference. Available controls depend on the exact version you are using.

  • Minimize: Use a nickname and avoid entering sensitive information.
  • Review: Open the History panel to see records stored by the app.
  • Clear history: Use the Clear control in the History panel.
  • Reset preferences: Clear local site data in your browser to remove the saved name and accent color.
  • Stop using the app: Close the page; if desired, remove its local storage through browser settings.

Depending on your location and the way MCC is hosted, you may have legal rights to request access, correction, deletion, objection, restriction, or other privacy remedies. Because this standalone version does not maintain a central account database of your local records, those rights may need to be exercised through your device or the relevant hosting provider. This policy does not limit any rights that applicable law grants you.

12. Third-party services and external links

The supplied standalone calculator is intended to work without third-party scripts or external services for its core calculations. If a distributor adds links, ads, embedded content, authentication, cloud services, analytics, or payment processing, those services may collect information under their own policies.

We do not control the privacy, security, or content practices of independent third parties. Review their notices before sharing information with them. The appearance of a third-party name or link in a modified version does not mean that the standalone MCC file operates or controls that service.

13. Hosting, downloads and server logs

When MCC is hosted publicly, a hosting provider may automatically process technical request information to deliver the file, protect the service, troubleshoot errors, prevent abuse, or measure service reliability. Typical server-side logs can include IP address, timestamp, requested resource, status code, and user-agent information. The exact fields and retention periods depend on the provider and configuration.

The app's page-level network restrictions do not prevent a server from receiving the initial request needed to deliver a hosted file. If you download the file and run it locally, the host may still have logged the download request, but the app's later calculations are processed in the local page in the supplied version.

For questions about hosting logs, review the privacy and data-retention information published by the service that hosts your copy. If you are the site operator, provide your own accurate contact details, data-controller identity where required, and any required legal disclosures.

14. International use and legal compliance

You may access MCC from different countries or regions. Privacy laws and terminology vary by location. This policy describes the behavior of the supplied standalone file at a general level and is not a statement that every legal obligation is satisfied in every jurisdiction.

If you operate or distribute MCC commercially, you are responsible for reviewing the laws that apply to your audience and deployment, including any rules on privacy notices, children's data, cookies, consumer disclosures, accessibility, and data security. Update this policy to reflect the actual operator, actual data practices, and local legal requirements.

15. Changes to this policy

This policy may be updated when the app changes, new features are added, hosting arrangements change, or legal requirements evolve. The effective date at the top indicates the date of this document version. A newer version should describe material changes clearly.

If new features introduce remote data collection, accounts, cloud synchronization, analytics, advertising, or payments, the operator should update this policy before enabling those features and provide any notices or choices required by law. Do not rely on this policy for a substantially modified version without reviewing it.

16. Contact and privacy requests

If this page is published as part of an official MCC website, the site operator should provide a monitored contact address or privacy-request form here. No verified privacy contact details were supplied with this standalone file, so this template intentionally does not invent an email address, phone number, business address, or legal entity.

Site owner action: Before publishing commercially, replace this paragraph with the real operator name and a monitored contact method. If applicable law requires a data controller, representative, grievance officer, or other contact, include the accurate details and process.

If you are using a copy distributed by someone else, contact that publisher or the hosting platform for questions about its deployment and data practices.

17. Important notice

This document is a privacy-policy template describing the supplied MCC HTML file based on its visible implementation. It is not a legal opinion, security certification, audit of the hosting environment, or guarantee that every distributed copy behaves identically. The site owner should verify the final code and hosting configuration and obtain qualified legal advice when needed.

In case of a conflict between this page and the actual behavior of a modified version, the operator must investigate and update the notice so that it accurately reflects the product. Never describe a feature as local-only, anonymous, encrypted, or free of tracking unless the complete deployed system supports that statement.

18. Data-flow overview

This section gives a practical overview of how information moves through the supplied standalone HTML version. It describes the intended flow of the delivered file, not every browser, device, operating-system, hosting, or network process outside the app's control.

When you first open the page

If you open a hosted copy, your browser first requests the HTML document from the hosting service. That request necessarily reaches the server that delivers the file and may be recorded in ordinary server logs. If you open a downloaded copy, the initial download may already have been recorded by the site or service from which you obtained it. Once the supplied page is running, its restrictive page policy is designed to block the page from making network connections.

When you enter a value

Calculator inputs are used by the page's JavaScript to calculate a displayed result. The supplied version is not designed to send the entered values to a remote calculator service. Avoid treating this design as permission to enter confidential data: the browser, device, extensions, screen recording tools, accessibility tools, or other software on the device may operate independently of the app.

When you save history or preferences

The app may write a limited set of values, including the display name, calculation history and accent-color preference, to browser local storage. This storage remains on the browser/device environment rather than being placed in an MCC account database by the supplied version. A person who has access to the same browser profile may also have access to those values.

When you clear history

The History control removes the calculation-history records that the app manages. Clearing history does not automatically remove every other local preference, browser cache, operating-system backup, browser sync copy, screenshot, or hosting log. Use the browser's own site-data controls if you also want to remove the saved name and color preference.

ActionExpected app behaviorWhat may be outside app control
Open hosted pageLoads the calculator page.Hosting provider request logs and network infrastructure.
Perform a calculationComputes and displays a result in the page.Device monitoring, extensions, screenshots or other software.
Save historyStores supported history records locally in the browser.Access by other users of the same browser profile or device.
Change theme colorSaves the color preference locally.Browser storage cleanup, profile sync behavior or device access.
Clear historyRemoves history records managed by the app.Other storage, copies, screenshots and provider logs.

19. Legal bases and purposes

Where a privacy law requires a legal basis for personal-data processing, the appropriate basis depends on who operates the copy, where the operator and user are located, and which features are enabled. The supplied standalone file does not identify a legal entity or establish a universal legal basis for every possible deployment. The following are explanations for a site operator to review, not a claim that a particular legal basis applies in every situation.

  • Providing the calculator: processing values you enter so the page can return the calculation you requested may be necessary to provide the feature you chose to use.
  • Remembering your preferences: local storage of a name or theme preference may support the function you expect when you revisit the page. If local-storage consent or notice rules apply to your deployment, the operator should provide the required choice or notice.
  • Maintaining security: a hosting provider may process technical logs to deliver files, prevent abuse, diagnose faults, or protect infrastructure, according to its own terms and applicable law.
  • Legal obligations: an operator may need to retain or disclose limited information where required by a valid legal obligation. Such obligations do not arise from the standalone HTML file itself.

The supplied page is not designed to create a marketing profile, run targeted advertising, sell local calculation history, or build a cross-site identity. If the operator later adds advertising, analytics, account services, cloud storage, remote AI, payments, or other integrations, the operator must reassess the data flows and legal bases before activating those features.

20. Privacy requests process

Because the supplied version stores its main saved preferences and history in the browser, there is generally no central MCC account record for an operator to search, correct, or delete on your behalf. You can usually inspect and remove this information directly in the same browser profile. A hosted website operator may still hold technical server logs or other records associated with site operation.

How to make a request to the correct party

  1. Identify whether you are using the original standalone file, a copy hosted on an MCC website, or a modified version distributed by another party.
  2. For local name, color, and history data, use the app controls and browser site-data settings described in Section 8.
  3. For server logs or information held by a website operator, contact the operator using its published privacy contact details.
  4. For information held by a third-party host or service, consult that provider's privacy notice and request process.
  5. Describe the request clearly, but do not send passwords, payment details, government ID numbers, or other unnecessary sensitive information in an ordinary email.

Depending on applicable law, requests may include access, correction, deletion, portability, objection, restriction, or withdrawal of consent. The scope, deadlines, identity-verification requirements and exceptions differ by jurisdiction. An operator should respond according to the law that actually applies and should not request more identity information than is reasonably necessary to process the request safely.

If an operator cannot locate a requested item because it was never collected centrally or has already been deleted, it should explain that limitation accurately. This policy does not remove or reduce any mandatory rights provided by applicable law.

21. Security incident and breach response

The app includes technical protections, but no software or hosting arrangement can promise zero risk. A security incident could involve unauthorized device access, a compromised hosting account, a malicious modified copy, a vulnerable browser, or exposure of data held by a separate provider. The appropriate response depends on the incident and the party that controls the affected system.

If you believe information has been exposed, stop entering sensitive information, close the page if appropriate, and secure the affected device and browser account. If the issue concerns a hosted website, notify that site's operator using its verified contact channel. If the issue concerns a browser extension, operating system, or hosting account, contact the relevant provider as well.

A site operator should have a proportionate incident-response plan that includes assessing the facts, containing the issue, preserving necessary evidence, correcting the cause, and determining whether notices to affected users or authorities are required by law. The operator should not state that a breach occurred—or that no breach occurred—without an appropriate factual basis.

The standalone file does not provide a centralized breach-detection service, account monitoring, device antivirus, or incident-response team. Any such services would need to be separately provided and accurately described.

22. Data accuracy, integrity and calculation limitations

Personal data and calculation values can be inaccurate because of typing errors, unexpected input formats, rounding, browser differences, or a defect in a calculator formula. The app is a general-purpose utility and should not be treated as the authoritative record for a financial, legal, medical, engineering, tax, academic assessment, or safety-critical decision.

  • Check the units, signs, decimal places, dates and assumptions you enter.
  • Review the displayed result before copying or relying on it.
  • For high-impact decisions, verify the method and result independently using a trusted source or qualified professional.
  • Do not assume that a history entry is a complete audit trail. History may retain a displayed summary rather than every original input, assumption, or intermediate step.
  • Do not assume a result is backed up. Browser storage can be cleared, corrupted, unavailable, or lost when a profile or device changes.

Where the app displays a history item, the stored value is intended to help you recall recent use. It is not a certified financial ledger, immutable log, official invoice, or proof that a transaction occurred. Users remain responsible for checking important calculations and retaining any records they legally or practically need.

23. Accessibility, shared devices and account safety

Privacy depends partly on how a device is shared and configured. If you use MCC on a school, library, workplace, family, internet-café, or other shared computer, someone else may be able to open the same browser profile and see saved history or preferences. Clearing the app's history is helpful but does not remove screenshots, downloaded copies, clipboard contents, browser-level records, or information saved by other software.

  • Prefer a separate operating-system or browser profile when a device is shared.
  • Sign out of the browser profile itself when finished, where applicable.
  • Do not save sensitive information in names, calculator fields, or history summaries.
  • Review browser extensions and install only extensions you trust.
  • Lock your device when you leave it unattended.
  • If using a public computer, consider closing the page and clearing site data after use, while remembering that public-device administrators may have other monitoring capabilities.

Accessibility features, screen readers, clipboard managers, keyboard utilities, remote-desktop software, and device-level assistive technologies may process what appears on screen or what you copy. Those tools are outside the calculator's direct control and may have their own privacy settings. This notice is not intended to discourage accessibility tools; it is a reminder to review settings on shared or sensitive devices.

24. Responsibilities of website owners and distributors

If you publish, host, rebrand, embed, or distribute MCC, you become responsible for checking that your deployed product and this notice match. The supplied privacy policy is a starting point for transparency; it is not a substitute for the operator's own legal review or operational controls.

Before launch, a site operator should:

  • Identify the actual person or organization operating the service and provide a monitored privacy contact.
  • Check the final HTML, JavaScript, headers, hosting configuration, and every third-party integration.
  • Remove statements that no longer match the product, including claims about local storage, network restrictions, accounts, analytics, or retention.
  • Explain any hosting logs, support inboxes, analytics, advertising, payment processors, cloud storage, AI endpoints, or account databases that are actually used.
  • Set and verify appropriate HTTP security headers on the live HTTPS site. A meta policy inside HTML does not replace all response headers.
  • Set realistic retention periods for logs and support records, restrict staff access, and document who can access information.
  • Provide any required notices, consent controls, grievance contact, representative, children's privacy process, or other disclosures for the applicable jurisdiction.
  • Review the policy whenever the product, operator, hosting provider, or data practices change.

Do not claim that data is encrypted, anonymous, deleted permanently, inaccessible to all third parties, or impossible to leak unless those statements have been verified for the entire relevant system. A browser-only design can reduce remote data flows, but it cannot control every component of the user's device or the hosting environment.

25. Definitions

  • App or supplied version: the standalone Math Center Calculator HTML file distributed with this policy, as distinct from a modified or integrated version.
  • Browser local storage: a browser feature that lets a website origin save small amounts of data on the user's device. It is not automatically encrypted and is not the same as cloud storage.
  • Calculation history: the list of recent calculation summaries the app saves to help a user recall prior results.
  • Personal information or personal data: information that identifies, relates to, describes, or can reasonably be linked to an identifiable person under the law that applies.
  • Hosting provider: a company or service that delivers the page or files to a browser and may process technical request information.
  • Third party: a person, company, service, or organization separate from the user and the operator of the copy being used.
  • Security header: an instruction delivered by a web server with an HTTP response to help browsers handle content more safely. Some security behaviors cannot be fully enforced using HTML meta tags alone.
  • Modified copy: a version whose code, hosting, integrations, storage behavior, branding, or data collection differs from the supplied standalone file.

These definitions are included for readability and may not replace formal definitions in the privacy laws applicable to a particular deployment.

26. Publication checklist

This policy should be reviewed before it is presented as the final legal notice for a public website. Use the checklist below to verify the real deployment rather than assuming that a local test guarantees the behavior of the published website.

  • Confirm that the displayed operator name and privacy contact are correct.
  • Confirm which fields are written to local storage and how the app's Clear History feature behaves.
  • Confirm that the deployed version does not include unlisted analytics, external scripts, remote fonts, remote APIs, advertising pixels, or embedded services.
  • Check the actual HTTP response headers on the live site, including Content Security Policy, Referrer Policy, Permissions Policy and framing restrictions.
  • Review the host's own logging, retention, support and abuse-prevention practices.
  • Verify whether local-storage notice or consent requirements apply to the intended audience.
  • Update this page if accounts, cloud synchronization, remote AI, payments, subscriptions, telemetry, or third-party integrations are introduced.
  • Provide accessible ways to read the policy and contact the operator.
  • Keep a dated copy of each material policy revision and make material changes understandable to users.
  • Seek qualified legal advice when the app is used commercially, processes children's data, or serves users in jurisdictions with specific privacy requirements.
Important for operators: A privacy policy describes practices; it does not itself create technical privacy protections. Configure the software and hosting to match the promises made here.

27. Plain-language summary

The supplied MCC file is designed to perform calculations in the browser and to keep a limited set of preferences and history records in browser local storage. It is not designed to send calculator inputs or saved local history to an MCC cloud database. The page includes restrictions intended to prevent its own code from initiating network connections in supporting browsers.

However, opening a hosted page can generate server logs, browser extensions and device software operate independently, local storage is not an encrypted vault, and a modified version may behave differently. You can clear history in the app and remove saved preferences through browser site-data settings. If you need to ask about hosting records, contact the operator of the website where you accessed the page.

Use a nickname if you prefer not to enter your real name, avoid sensitive information, keep your device secure, and independently verify results that matter. The site operator must keep this policy aligned with the actual deployed version and applicable law.
